procedure_column: Zhang et al. 2022 (GCA 323) Iron meteorites Raster mapping + Spot (Ge) ns-LA-SF-ICP-MS Florida State University

Procedure Name.cell: Zhang et al. (2022) Iron Meteorite LA-ICP-MS v1
Procedure Name.value: Zhang et al. (2022) Iron Meteorite LA-ICP-MS v1

Procedure Author.cell: Zhang, Chabot, Rubin, Humayun et al.
Procedure Author.value: Zhang, Chabot, Rubin, Humayun et al.

Laboratory.cell: Plasma Analytical Facility, Florida State University, Tallahassee FL, USA
Laboratory.value: Plasma Analytical Facility, Florida State University, Tallahassee FL, USA

Procedure Reference(s).cell: Zhang et al. (2022) GCA 323, 202–219; Humayun (2012) for standardization
Procedure Reference(s).value: Zhang et al. (2022) GCA 323, 202–219; Humayun (2012) for standardization

Coupling Description.cell: Quantitative analysis, mixed WDS/EDS element mapping, and characterization of mineral phases from NWA 1911 and Zinder [Section 2.5]
Coupling Description.value: Quantitative analysis, mixed WDS/EDS element mapping, and characterization of mineral phases from NWA 1911 and Zinder [Section 2.5]

Target Material.cell: Iron meteorite metal (kamacite + taenite); pyroxene-bearing pallasite metal

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Whole sample (polished specimen surface) > Region of interest (raster) — irons "were analyzed using a raster scan over a few millimeters" with a 50 μm beam, and compositions are reported as "raster averages" per specimen (Table 3, pp.4–5); Ge comes from a set of five 150 μm spots on five of the irons (p.4)
Sampling Unit Type.value: Whole sample (polished specimen surface) > Region of interest (raster)

Sample Preparation Method.cell: Polished slabs of the irons; a mount of Zinder and a section of NWA 1911 for the pallasites (§2.1); no acid treatment is described for the LA-ICP-MS specimens
Sample Preparation Method.value: Polished slabs of the irons; a mount of Zinder and a section of NWA 1911 for the pallasites (§2.1); no acid treatment is described for the LA-ICP-MS specimens

Sampling Unit Selection Criteria.cell: Representativeness of the exsolution banding — the raster "yielded more representative sampling of the kamacite-taenite banding", and where it "failed to yield useful Ge abundances for Klamath Falls ... To obtain more precise Ge, a set of five 150 μm spots were analyzed ... on five of the irons" (p.4)

Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.cell: Electron-microprobe mapping, for the pallasites only — "Quantitative analysis, mixed WDS/EDS element mapping, and characterization of the mineral phases from NWA 1911 and Zinder were performed" on the Bruker instrument, producing Si, Al, Cr, Fe, Mg, Ca, Na, P and Ni maps "along with backscattered electron (BSE) maps" at 6 μm per pixel (pp.5–6); for the irons the paper states only that the rasters were "taken on polished surfaces" (p.5)
Pre-Analysis Imaging and Screening.value: Electron-microprobe mapping, for the pallasites only

Detector Configuration.cell: Triple mode detection at 65% duty cycle — 'triple mode detection at 65% duty cycle' (§2.2)
Detector Configuration.value: Triple mode detection at 65% duty cycle

Data Processing Software(s).cell: N — paper only states "standardization techniques followed those of Humayun (2012)"; no software named

Laser Spot Geometry.cell: raster: 50 µm beam spot; Ge spots: 150 µm — §2.2

Laser Spot Path / Ablation Mode.cell: raster: raster scan over a few millimeters; Ge spots: spot — §2.2

value.value: raster scan over a few millimeters

Ablation Duration per Spot.cell: 20 s for the Ge spots — 'analyzed at 50 Hz for 20 s' (§2.2); the raster duration is not stated

Transect Rate, Mapping Rate or Step Size.cell: raster: 10 µm/s; Ge spots: N/A — 'scanned at 10 µm/s' (§2.2)

Target Species.cell: P, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Ga, Ge, As, Mo, Ru, Rh, Pd, Sn, Sb, W, Re, Os, Ir, Pt, Au — the 23 elements whose peaks were acquired (§2.2)

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species
Monitored Masses.cell: ³¹P → P; ⁵¹V → V; ⁵³Cr → Cr; ⁵⁵Mn → Mn; ⁵⁷Fe → Fe; ⁵⁹Co → Co; ⁶⁰Ni → Ni; ⁶³Cu → Cu; ⁷¹Ga → Ga; ⁷⁴Ge → Ge; ⁷⁵As → As; ⁹⁵Mo → Mo; ¹⁰²Ru → Ru; ¹⁰³Rh → Rh; ¹⁰⁶Pd → Pd; ¹²⁰Sn → Sn; ¹²¹Sb → Sb; ¹⁸²W → W; ¹⁸⁵Re → Re; ¹⁹⁰Os → Os; ¹⁹³Ir → Ir; ¹⁹⁵Pt → Pt; ¹⁹⁷Au → Au — 'were used to acquire the peaks 31P, 51V, ... and 197Au' (§2.2)

Reported Variables and Units.cell: P, Fe, Co, Ni (mg/g); V, Cr, Mn, Cu, Ga, Ge, As, Mo, Ru, Rh, Pd, Sn, Sb, W, Re, Os, Ir, Pt, Au (µg/g) — abundances in metal, Table 3 (raster averages) with spot averages in Appendix 2; 'Concentrations below detection limits are not shown'

Inter-Pass Data Dependency.cell: N — the Ge value combines both passes (Combination Method), but no pass uses another's data

Number of Replicates.cell: N — 'a set of five 150 µm spots were analyzed ... on five of the irons, including both slabs of Klamath Falls' (§2.2)

Acquisition Pass.cell: raster; Ge spots — 'Irons were analyzed using a raster scan over a few millimeters'; 'To obtain more precise Ge, a set of five 150 µm spots were analyzed at 50 Hz for 20 s on five of the irons' (§2.2)

Internal Standard Approach.cell: N — 'Standardization techniques followed those of Humayun (2012)' (§2.2)

Internal Standard Element.cell: N — not stated; standardization follows Humayun (2012)

Elemental Fractionation Correction.cell: N — 'Standardization techniques followed those of Humayun (2012)' (§2.2); the standards are under Primary Calibration Standard Name

Pulse/Analog Detector Nonlinearity Corre.cell: N — 'triple mode detection at 65% duty cycle' (§2.2); a cross-calibration is not described

Spectral Interference Corrections Applie.cell: N — the 150 µm Ge spots produced 'a sufficiently bright beam to resolve Ge from background argide interferences' (§2.2); no correction is described

Interfering Species.cell: ⁷⁴Ge: background argides; other: N — overcome by the brighter 150 µm Ge spots, not corrected (§2.2)

Interference Correction Method.cell: N — the argide interference on Ge was avoided with a brighter beam, not corrected

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Partially — the rule stated is one of combination rather than rejection: for Ge, Sb, Re, Os and Ir the reported value is "calculated from the mean of the spot average (Appendix 2) and the raster average in this table" (Table 3 note, p.4). No acceptance or rejection rule for individual results is stated. The exclusion of "Binya and Fitzwater Pass ... from the fractional-crystallization modeling of group IIIF" (p.5) is an interpretive exclusion downstream of the reported values, not a rule about which results make them

Combination Method.cell: Ge, Sb, Re, Os, Ir: mean of the spot average and the raster average; other: raster average — Table 3 title 'Compositions (raster averages)'; note: 'calculated from the mean of the spot average (Appendix 2) and the raster average in this table'

value.value: mean of the spot average and the raster average

Primary Calibration Standard Name.cell: all [Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, As, W, Au: North Chile (Filomena, IIAB) and NIST SRM 1263a V-Cr steel; Ga, Ge: North Chile (Filomena, IIAB); Ru, Rh, Pd, Re, Os, Ir, Pt: Hoba (IVB); V, Cr, Mo: NIST SRM 1263a V-Cr steel; other: N] — 'The standard used for Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Ga, Ge, As, W, and Au is North Chile (Filomena; IIAB) (Wasson et al., 1989), and the standard for Ru, Rh, Pd, Re, Os, Ir, and Pt is Hoba (IVB) (Walker et al., 2008). NIST SRM 1263a V-Cr steel was also used for V, Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, As, Mo, W, and Au' (§2.2)

value.value: North Chile (Filomena, IIAB) and NIST SRM 1263a V-Cr steel

Detection Limit.cell: N — 'Concentrations below detection limits are not shown' (Table 3); the limits are not given

Counting Statistics Error.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Metho.cell: N — compared with NAA on the same irons rather than a standard: differences 'mostly ... within the range of ±40%', within ±10% for Ni, Co and Ga, up to 30% for Au and As, and W in Cerro del Inca 4.39 ng/g by LA-ICP-MS against 1.06 ng/g by INAA (§2.3)

Additional Notes.cell: The raster pass gives the 23-element dataset; a separate set of 150 µm spots on five irons gives more precise Ge, since the raster 'failed to yield useful Ge abundances for Klamath Falls' (§2.2)
Additional Notes.value: The raster pass gives the 23-element dataset; a separate set of 150 µm spots on five irons gives more precise Ge, since the raster 'failed to yield useful Ge abundances for Klamath Falls' (§2.2)
